projects.name: Solar + Energy Storage on Garage
projects.description: Install 5-7 solar panels on south-facing garage roof face (20x12 ft, ~2-2.8 kW) plus battery storage. Solar = standalone ROI investment (~5yr payback at $0.42/kWh). Battery = generator alternative (no lot space for generator). 30% federal ITC applies to both when paired.
projects.notes: DESIGN: South garage face only. 5 portrait panels = 2.0 kW; 7 mixed = 2.8 kW. ~3,200-4,500 kWh/yr production (20-26% offset). All-in after ITC: solar ~$9-10k, battery ~$9-10k. VENDORS: Sunergy (sunergy.com) — EnergySage 2026 CA Installer of Year, Enphase Platinum, no door-to-door. NRG Clean Power (nrgcleanpower.com) — Diamond Certified, 35yr, San Mateo County, 40yr warranty. Tesla Energy (tesla.com/energy) — online only. AVOID: Sunrun.

tasks.title: Analyze energy usage and size system
tasks.notes: 17,178 kWh/yr at $0.42/kWh avg. Target: 5-7 panels south garage face (20x12 ft) = 2-2.8 kW. ~5yr payback after ITC.

tasks.title: Research and shortlist solar installers
tasks.notes: Shortlist: Sunergy (sunergy.com, Enphase Platinum, no door-to-door), NRG Clean Power (nrgcleanpower.com, Diamond Certified, San Mateo County), Tesla Energy (tesla.com/energy, online only). Avoid Sunrun.

tasks.title: Contact installers for quotes
tasks.notes: Spec: south garage face (20x12 ft, 5-7 panels, ~2-2.8 kW), paired battery (Enphase IQ or Powerwall 3), detached garage sub-panel interconnect. Ask each for: $/W, panel brand, inverter type, battery spec, warranty, timeline, ITC total. Request free shade/LIDAR analysis.

tasks.title: Compare quotes and select installer
tasks.notes: Prefer Enphase microinverters over string inverter. Compare $/W, battery spec, warranty, timeline. 30% ITC on full system incl. battery.

tasks.title: Confirm ITC timing — credit files in year PTO is granted
tasks.notes: 30% federal ITC on Form 5695. Claimed in tax year Permission to Operate granted by PG&E. Battery qualifies only when solar-paired. Plan install timing accordingly.

insights.summary: The simultaneous sleep completion at 00:12, paired with a perfectly stable device count (23-25) and zero camera motion for over three hours, confirms the house is in a secure, undisturbed sleep state; the high device count is consistent with background IoT traffic rather than human activity, indicating no unusual events or security concerns.

The highly stable 23–25 device count combined with zero camera motion at 2 AM strongly indicates background IoT/Wi-Fi infrastructure rather than active human presence, clarifying that the earlier presence flags are likely false positives and the home is in a normal overnight state.

The sustained high device count (21–24) combined with zero camera activity at 1:24 AM, immediately following the adults' wake-up, suggests unaccounted occupancy in camera-blind zones. This connectivity-presence mismatch creates a security blind spot that warrants verifying door locks and guest status before the day begins.

The simultaneous ~9.5-hour sleep completion for both adults, paired with a stable high device count and zero camera motion, confirms the household is securely resting; the elevated device count is consistent with background IoT and charging phones rather than unauthorized presence.

The sustained count of 21–23 connected devices significantly exceeds the household's expected footprint, especially with zero camera activity late on a weekday evening. This pattern strongly suggests unlogged guests, a network misconfiguration causing false presence detection, or neighbor device bleed, warranting a quick verification to rule out security or configuration issues.

The sustained presence of 21–22 mobile devices combined with zero camera activity on a weekday evening strongly indicates either a network counting artifact (IoT devices misidentified as phones) or that the security cameras are offline, leaving the home's actual status unverified.

The sustained count of 19–22 devices paired with zero camera motion on a weekday evening strongly indicates a presence detection anomaly or network tracking error, as it is implausible for so many extra people to remain completely undetected by cameras while actively connected to the network.

The consistent presence of 19–23 devices alongside zero camera motion on a weekday evening strongly suggests either a large, stationary gathering (like a movie night or dinner party) or a tracking anomaly where static IoT devices are being falsely counted as present. This matters because it deviates significantly from the household's normal 4-person routine and warrants a quick confirmation of guest status or presence system calibration.

The sustained high device count (16–23) with zero camera motion on a weekday evening strongly indicates either a large group of guests settled in a non-camera area or the presence system miscounting smart home IoT devices as mobile phones. Verifying guest status or adjusting device classification thresholds will clarify if this is a normal gathering or a network configuration issue.

The sustained 16-19 device count paired with zero camera motion on a weekday strongly suggests either unreported guests gathered in a camera-blind area or smart home/IoT devices being miscounted as mobile phones, warranting a quick verification to ensure home security and accurate automation baselines.
